newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Wheelock building 21st century landbank.
newsitem.headline: Wheelock building 21st century landbank.

text.p: Wheelock and Company Ltd said on Thursday the company was set to realise a sustained period of value expansion, supported by a new earnings growth cycle, and a landbank that would carry the group beyond 2001.

"The gradual recognition of profit from the group's development properties supported by ...income generated from substantial rental billings...will provide the group with a new cycle of earnings growth," chairman Gonzaga Li said in a statement released with the company's final results.

Wheelock announced a group profit of HK$2.54 billion for the year ended March 1997, a 3.1 percent rise over HK$2.46 billion in 1996. Earnings per share rose to HK$1.255 from HK$1.22 in the previous year.
While the group had accumulated sufficient landbank for development beyond 2001, it was looking for opportunities to replenish it, Li said.

The company's principal associate, The Wharf (Holdings) Ltd, had a portfolio of investment and development property of about 20 million sq feet in Hong Kong and more than 10 million sq feet in China, which would lead the group's development through the next decade, Li said
Wharf is 46 percent held by Wheelock and accounts for about 44 percent of Wheelock's earnings, analysts said.
In the coming year, the company would see increased rental income from its Plaza Hollywood which opened this month.
"Futures sales of the five residential blocks behind this mall are expected to yield a substantial profit," the chairman's statement said.
In Singapore, plans were underway to redevelop The Marco Polo Hotel and the group is actively sourcing sites to enlarge its existing landbank," the statement said.
Wheelock holds 74.46 percent of Singapore-listed Marco Polo Development Ltd.

The company reported an increase in profit before exceptionals, including those of associates, of 43.5 percent, boosted by the consolidation of the results of New Asia Realty and Trust Co Ltd, the company's earnings announcement said.
New Asia, previously an associate company, became a subsidiary on August 14, 1996. Wheelock holds 72 percent of New Asia.
Subsidiary Wheelock Properties saw a strong upturn in its sales income, launching a total of 12 property sales programmes during the year and recording 800 units sold, Li said.

An annual revaluation of the company's and its associate companies' investment properties raised the group's consolidated net asset value to HK$22.63 per share as at the end of March 1997, compared with HK$19.43 per share at end-March 1996, the chairman's statement said.
